introStyles: problem-led: Open with the specific problem the business owner is facing — describe it vividly. Then show the impact on their business before introducing the solution.
outcome-led: Open with the positive result the business could have — a concrete picture of what changes when they get this right. Then show the gap between where they are now and that outcome.
trust-led: Open by establishing the landscape — who is succeeding locally and why. Position the reader as someone who already understands quality, then introduce the service as the natural next step.

local-competition-led: Open by naming the competitive reality of this specific area — how many similar businesses are online and what separates the ones winning enquiries. Then position the service as the lever that changes that.
visibility-led: Open with the risk of being invisible online when local customers are actively searching. Then show how a stronger website improves discoverability.
conversion-led: Open with the idea that traffic is wasted if the website does not convert. Then explain how design, layout and messaging turn visitors into enquiries.
credibility-led: Open with the importance of first impressions. Show how customers judge trust, professionalism and reliability before they make contact.
modernisation-led: Open by describing the problem of an outdated website. Position the service as a practical upgrade that improves trust, speed and performance.
customer-journey-led: Open with how a customer searches, compares and decides. Then show how the website needs to support each step of that journey.
growth-led: Open with the wider business goal — more enquiries, better visibility and stronger local positioning. Then frame the website as a growth asset.
ctaStyles: quote-focused: Drive toward a specific quote or proposal. Make it easy and low-commitment — just a brief description of what they need.
consultation-focused: Offer a short discovery conversation. Position it as a chance to get clarity, not a sales pitch.
low-pressure: Remove all pressure — no obligation, no hard sell. Emphasise that the first step is just a quick conversation or message.
growth-focused: Connect the CTA to the business outcome they want — more enquiries, more visibility, more growth. Make taking action feel like a business decision, not a purchase.
audit-focused: Invite the user to request a quick website review. Position it as a useful first step before deciding what to do next.
planning-focused: Offer to create a clear plan for improving the website. Emphasise clarity, priorities and next steps.
pricing-focused: Encourage the user to request clear pricing based on their requirements. Emphasise transparency and no guesswork.
comparison-focused: Invite the user to compare what they have now with what a stronger website could achieve.
project-start-focused: Encourage the user to start the project by sending basic details. Keep the next step simple.
expert-advice-focused: Offer practical advice from someone who understands local business websites and search visibility.
